results.correct_value: Camping in Upper Royal Basin is permitted: it has no designated sites, camping there is on bare ground or gravel only, and the permit is arranged through the park's Wilderness Information Center rather than booked online like Royal Lake.
results.evidence: The park's own wilderness permit system lists 'Upper Royal Basin (No Campfires)' as a bookable camp area, and its Royal Lake entry says the Royal Lake sites are at the lake, not in the Upper Basin, and that to camp in the Upper Basin you contact the WIC at (360) 565-3100. A backpacking write-up quotes the park rule that Upper Royal Basin has no designated campsites and camping is only on bare ground or gravel, avoiding Imperial Tarn, and that its permit is by phone to the WIC; a WTA trip-report search snippet carries the same rule. The NPS Royal Basin page lists only Royal Creek, Lower Royal Meadow and Royal Lake as designated-site areas, which is consistent (the upper basin has no designated sites) rather than a ban. The three fields saying camping is not permitted in Upper Royal Basin are wrong; bivy[0] is right and is not touched.

results.correct_value: The Needles' rock is better than the pillow lava typical of much of the Olympics, but it is still loose and rockfall-prone.
results.evidence: A Mount Deception route page says the Needles crags hold rock of much higher quality, in contrast to the pillow lava that makes for poor climbing across much of the range (the Mount Deception article likewise calls its pillow lava poor climbing). The Royal Basin area page says that, like all Olympic rock, its chossiness is part of its appeal, and the row's hazards, obj_haz, watch_out and seasonal_hazards all call the rock loose. Both are true in their frames; the beta was reworded so the relative claim no longer reads as a denial of the loose-rock hazard.
